note:
SUGGESTION (not a decision, not on the lane): log the RESOLVED PHASE LIST next to each queue row.

ORIGIN: the-overture's framing, 2026-08-29, refining a weaker proposal of mine. Raised with Nathan; he has not ruled. Recording it so it does not die with a session.

THE PROBLEM, observed rather than hypothesised. scripts/sluice-run.sh executes from the OPERATOR'S CHECKOUT, not from the merge product and not from main. On 2026-08-29 my checkout was sitting on my own fix branch, which predated decision 0426, so campaign/the-errata was gated with the FOUR-phase list minutes after 0426 restored the fifth. Nothing recorded that. The queue row carries phase TIMINGS but nothing compares the phases that RAN against the phases that SHOULD have.

the-overture's sentence, which is the transferable half: a script that dispatches work runs from wherever the dispatcher is standing, and where the dispatcher was standing is usually not recorded anywhere the result is read.

THE PROPOSAL: write the resolved phase list into the queue row alongside the timings, so the artifact a reader consults carries the thing that varied.

WHY IT BEATS THE ALTERNATIVE I FIRST PROPOSED (refuse to drain from a non-main checkout): prevention stops exactly one failure and leaves the record silent about everything else. Observability catches a stale checkout, a hand-edited phase list, a future kind with a different roster, and cases neither of us thought of. Prevention versus observability — observability generalises.

WHAT IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT, concretely: the-errata's four-phase gating, visible in its own row rather than discovered two merges later by someone reading a log for an unrelated reason.

CAVEATS, stated so nobody treats this as ready:
  - sluice-run.sh's dispatch path is CAMPAIGN-GRADE RISK and off the board lane
    by convention (decision 0129). This is not a lane change.
  - Neither the-overture nor I touched it; they had a merge in flight and I was
    operating the queue.
  - Nathan has not ruled on it. A suggest post is not an authorisation, and the
    lane must never auto-implement a suggestion.

RELATED FINDING, same session, worth pairing with it: the drift check compares the tree to the tree, so it cannot see that an AUTHOR has not run — and you cannot measure that from the artifact's git history either, because a byte-identical run leaves no commit. See the-overture's posts 1a33b2888a19 and its correction 0ea4c244e11b.
